title.narrative: for promoting evidence use in the U.N. General Assembly and other international policy processes

description.narrative: Promoting the use of evidence in international policymaking is by no means easy. There is little consensus on almost every stage of the evidence-to-policy process. As a result, it is hard for policymakers and experts to make suggestions on how to engage with one another, how to tailor their policy questions and make relevant their research, how to work within each other’s institutional contexts, and to each other’s time scales. Challenges are definitional (what kinds of evidence count?), institutional (what kinds of evidence-to-policy mechanisms work?), and scalar (how do we translate our knowledge of national policy processes to the international realm?). To help break the logjam, this grant continues support to a project bringing together researchers from the U.K. and across sub-Saharan Africa (Benin, South Sudan, Tanzania, and South Africa) to better understand localized meanings of evidence and local experiences of evidence-to-policy institutionalization. The work includes leveraging the insights from the project into ongoing technical assistance to U.N. member states in support of their efforts to strengthen the evidence-informed policymaking interfaces of the U.N General Assembly, as well publication of the findings and case studies in multiple forums. (Strategy: Evidence-Informed Policymaking)
